instruction:
Cavity Mask + Invert + Dark-Gray Polypaint Fill

The file at C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\scene.obj contains a ZBrush Tool whose first (and only) SubTool, named BumpyBall, is a UV-sphere (48 longitudes x 24 latitudes, 1106 vertices, 1152 faces) whose surface has been radially displaced by a sinusoidal bump field. Peaks of the noise field are further from the origin (radius approx 1.1) and valleys or cavities are closer (radius approx 0.9). The mesh has no polypaint, no UVs, a single default polygroup, and no subdivision-level stack above the base mesh.

Load this OBJ into ZBrush. Use Mask By Cavity to concentrate a mask in the surface cavities, invert the mask so the cavities become the unmasked region, fill that region with a dark-gray polypaint (0.2, 0.2, 0.2), and export the result as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj with MRGB vertex colors preserved.

The exported C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\output.obj must satisfy:

- Exactly one SubTool, still named BumpyBall, with its base geometry unchanged.
- Every vertex line is in MRGB form `v x y z r g b`.
- The Pearson correlation between a geometric cavity proxy and per-vertex brightness `(r+g+b)\3` is < -0.6.
- The median brightness of the top-20% most-cavity vertices is at least 0.3 lower than the median brightness of the bottom-20% least-cavity vertices.
